findings: A1: ten of the eleven H2 sections are present and every one of the six rubric-parsed headings is spelled canonically. `## Build plan` is deliberately absent: prompts/generate_instruction.md section 2.1 removed it from the baseline because a numbered implementation sequence deletes the design work this benchmark measures. The prompt row predates that decision; cited, not rewritten.

B3: two of the three difficulty levers are emitted (`## Technical requirements`, `## Data model`). The third, `## Build plan`, is withheld by the same settled baseline rule as A1, so the variant records as intended rather than as a different difficulty.

C7: the grading window is deliberately exceeded. window_lint reports `past-slice` on core_features (14390), user_flow (4687) and ui_ux_notes (8465) against the 2500-char slice, and 31672 joined against 9000. The tasker asked for a fully detailed brief and accepted that the tail reaches the agent but not the judge; G33 fails nothing on length and judge_score never touches reward.

S2: 01-PRD.md lists ten must-have features against the prompt's 3-6 band. `config/corpus-targets.yaml` sets `companion_feature_cap: [6, 10]` for a companion-backed task and states that the 3-6 cap deletes the one input that makes such a task hard. The out-of-scope list is present and explicit.

BP-004: the Node setup script is fetched over HTTPS and piped to a shell with no checksum, so a mismatch cannot fail the build. It is inherited verbatim from the kit's own Dockerfile skeleton (prompts/docker_generator.md), which publishes no checksum for it; changing it unilaterally would diverge the corpus.
DEP-011: `[verifier].environment_mode = "separate"`, so the grader ships its own image from tests/Dockerfile and the agent image owes it no pinned Python grader package.
DEP-016: `[metadata].language = "python"`, so there is no compiled-language build stage that could COPY a host-resolved dependency cache.
DEP-017: `[metadata].language` is not `java`, so no JRE is owed in the final stage.

SEC-003: the image runs as root. The kit skeleton establishes no non-root user and the agent writes into /app during its session, so a non-root switch would break the documented workflow. Recorded rather than changed.
BENCH-002: this is not a trivial or smoke task, so the Trivial resource tier does not apply. BENCH-001 carries the Standard tier and passes.
INST-007: `instruction.md` is present, so the SPEC folder is not standing in for the brief.

SCHEMA-011: the file carries a `[delivery]` block that the section 11 canonical template does not list. stage-4-task-toml.md requires it on every new bundle and tools/validate_task.py (G2) validates it, so the template is the stale source here; emitting it is correct and G2 passes.

SCHEMA-013: section order follows the template except that `[delivery]` sits between `[verifier]` and `[[artifacts]]`, the position stage-4 documents and both shipped bundles use. Same root cause as SCHEMA-011.
SIGN-001: deprecated 2026-09-15 with the retirement of `[signoff]`; superseded by SIGN-004, which passes.
SIGN-002: deprecated 2026-09-15 with the retirement of `[signoff]`; superseded by SIGN-004, which passes.
SIGN-003: deprecated 2026-09-15 with the retirement of `[signoff]`; superseded by SIGN-004, which passes.
TAX-006: `language = "python"`, so the `any` escape is not in use.

VERIF-005: `[verifier].env` carries `APP_PUBLIC_URL = "${APP_PUBLIC_URL:-http://main:4173}"` rather than the template's `localhost:4173`. Under `environment_mode = "separate"` the verifier runs in its own container, where `localhost` is that container rather than the app; `main` is the compose service name the app answers on. The template default was written for shared mode.
VERIF-007: the task declares no payments and no storage slot, so there are no shared provider credentials to carry into `[verifier].env`.
